clue.text: Company vehicle covered by MOT in shot, burning

indicators.note: covered by says the vehicle sits inside the rearranged letters, which wrap round it
shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A firm's van wrapped up by its roadworthiness test gets torched in a burning shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' (ruined) rearranges MOT IN to MTION; the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Combustion is the chemical process of burning, so the noun sense of burning fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Fish with a tail end

parts.note: the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish described as having a tail end, as any fish has.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a musical piece, its concluding section or finale.

clue.text: One's unclear about heartless Liberal turning up after old woman

indicators.note: after places the reversed pieces behind the old woman

parts.note: in British slang one's 'old woman' can be one's mother, MUM

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Someone's speech is unclear about a dispirited Liberal Party politician turning up behind an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the I from LIB, leaving LB; RE + LB, 'turning up', gives BLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mumbler speaks indistinctly, so a mumbler is a person whose words are hard to make out.

clue.text: Fairytale character now swanning around?

parts.note: in Hans Christian Andersen's tale the despised cygnet grows into a beautiful swan, so it is now literally swanning around

explanation.surface: A storybook figure who is now idly showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swanning around' normally means drifting about aimlessly; here it means being a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andersen hero is an awkward cygnet mocked by farmyard birds who matures into a graceful adult swan.

clue.text: Experimental glassware needed? Try underground

parts.note: to test something is to try it
the Tube is the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: A lab worker asks whether glassware is needed and suggests trying underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is the narrow glass cylinder used in laboratory experiments.

clue.text: Cricketer, one that's often seen on the bottle?

definitions.meaning: a batsman who opens the innings

definitions.text: one that's often seen on the bottle?
definitions.meaning: a bottle ... is used on bottles

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is often seen drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the bottle' suggests heavy drinking, but the bottle opener is literally used on the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening batsmen start a cricket innings, and a bottle opener is the tool that removes caps.

clue.text: King Edward perhaps, returning in mood: upset

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A king Edward coming back in an upset mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' out; it is the hidden-word indicator, so it is added. King Edward is a British potato variety, and spud is slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato, and spud is the informal name for a potato.

clue.text: Disturbed couple imprisoning Northern composer

indicators.note: imprisoning says the rearranged letters hold the other piece inside
disturbed means upset or moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unsettled couple lock up a composer from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' turns COUPLE into POULEC, and 'imprisoning' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a twentieth-century French composer, one of the group known as Les Six.

clue.text: Fancy he's so loud touring student's small dwelling

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the student
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: L, for learner, is the usual crossword student; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A man boasts loudly while showing a student round a tiny home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges HE'S SO LOUD, and 'touring' puts L round inside to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doll's house is a miniature toy home, a very small dwelling for dolls.

clue.text: Protest, with one-third of listed building knocked down

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: one-third of says take the first two of the six letters in the word listed

parts.note: a shed is a building

explanation.surface: Protesters object as part of a listed building is knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed building' reads as a protected British building, but the words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish a structure is to pull it down, so demolished matches knocked down as a synonym.

clue.text: Part of ship found in English city

definitions.meaning: the main body of a ship
A port city in East Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A section of a vessel is located in an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The hull is a ship's watertight body, and Hull (Kingston upon Hull) is a city in Yorkshire.

clue.text: The sound of someone happy with killing?

indicators.note: of says the sound belongs to the someone, so the possessive comes first

parts.note: someone is a man, and the possessive gives man's
the sound of a happy person is laughter

explanation.surface: A happy person's laughter is heard alongside a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as MAN'S LAUGHTER, the sound someone happy makes; 'killing' also hints at laughing until you die.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is the crime of unlawfully causing death without premeditation, a kind of killing.

clue.text: Really pleased with flowers, half missing

indicators.note: half missing says only the front half of the word survives, the rest gone

parts.note: gladioli are flowers

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted with a bouquet, though half of the flowers are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: GLADIOLI keeps only its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be glad is to be happy or delighted, so glad stands for being truly pleased.

clue.text: Youngsters eat greens at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are in disorder

explanation.surface: Young people eat their vegetables while on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are people aged thirteen to nineteen, young people in their adolescent years.

clue.text: Second Conservative settling old scores: dealing in filth?

parts.note: avenging is taking revenge, settling old scores

explanation.surface: A second Tory politician takes revenge in a sleazy affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Scavenging means searching through refuse or rubbish for anything usable, handling dirt.

clue.text: Swan beset by problems with feet and inner ears?

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the swan sits inside the foot problems

parts.note: corns are painful patches of hard skin on the feet
a cob is a male swan

explanation.surface: A swan troubled by sore feet and inner-ear problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner ears' suggests anatomy; it means the core of an ear of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the woody central core of a maize ear on which the kernels grow.

clue.text: Tipsy choir hiding violent person

indicators.note: hiding says the answer lies concealed in the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A drunken choir is concealing a dangerous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A psycho is an informal word for a dangerously unstable person given to violence.

clue.text: Spelling group, perhaps, with a National Trust agreement

parts.note: a coven is a group of witches, who cast spells
NT stands for the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A spelling bee team strikes a deal with a heritage charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' means casting spells, not writing words; the National Trust is a British charity owning historic houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement or contract between parties.

clue.text: Manly Victor: one to get your hackles up?

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral one
to rile is to anger, to get your hackles up

explanation.surface: A macho man called Victor is one who makes people angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means having strong masculine qualities such as vigour and strength.

clue.text: Navy personnel's scores on TripAdvisor?

definitions.meaning: ordinary sailors in the navy who are not officers
the scores users give on review sites like TripAdvisor

explanation.surface: Sailors post reviews of their travels on a holiday website.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratings are non-commissioned sailors, and also the star scores reviewers award on websites.

clue.text: Wild consumers for a very long time eating rook!

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the phrase swallows the chess piece

parts.note: for ages means for a very long time
R is the chess notation abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Wild creatures that have been feeding for ages, including on a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild here describes what is consumed, not the consumers.
explanation.definitionFit: Foragers gather and eat food found growing naturally, so they consume what is wild.

clue.text: Artist regularly cried about entering Lego building

indicators.note: entering says the selected letters go inside the rearranged toy
building means putting together, so the toy's letters are assembled in a new order
regularly says take every other letter of the word cried

parts.note: C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An artist sobs regularly over a construction made of plastic bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes RE from cried; with C it goes inside ELGO, the Lego letters rearranged by 'building'.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance, famous for elongated figures.

clue.text: Charlie and Oscar, in this place, stick together

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Two men named Charlie and Oscar stay united right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold firmly together or form a unified whole.

clue.text: The take-home pay of fisherfolk?

parts.note: take-home pay is earnings after tax; fishermen bring home what comes in by the net

explanation.surface: A question about what people who fish earn after deductions.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for pay after tax is read as money coming in through the fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Net income means earnings after deductions, which is exactly what take-home pay is.

clue.text: Grand cooker? That's mad!

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
an Aga is a brand of large British range cooker

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a fancy stove is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is slang for crazy or senile, so it works as an informal synonym for mad.

clue.text: First of all, used trucks easily sell as such vehicles

indicators.note: first of all says take the opening letter of every following word

explanation.surface: Second-hand trucks are easy to sell as the kind of vehicle they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Utes, short for utility vehicles, is the Australian name for pickup trucks.
explanation.definitionFit: Utes are small pickup trucks, so they are the kind of vehicles the clue mentions.

clue.text: I could be given three directions for hostelries

parts.note: N, N and S are compass points: north, north and south

explanation.surface: Someone is told three routes to some pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Any compass point may be used, and repeated: here north twice and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are pubs or small hotels offering drink and lodging, which is what hostelries are.

clue.text: Detach case of machine in hollow unit

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
to part is to separate or detach

indicators.note: case of means the outer shell, the first and last letters of the word machine

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove the casing of a machine set into a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow unit' looks like a single phrase, but hollow is a piece and unit the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a division or section of an organisation, a unit within it.

clue.text: Cut good timber

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: An instruction to fell some decent wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep wound, a cut in the skin.

clue.text: Soldiers by the hundred?

parts.note: a Roman centurion commanded a century, a unit of about a hundred men

explanation.surface: Troops arriving in their hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the hundred' seems to mean in large numbers; it means each led a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Centurions were Roman army officers each in charge of a century, nominally one hundred soldiers.
